name: swarm-cursor
title: Swarm Cursor
description: Hundreds of white specks drift over a dark area and gather into a liquid, spinning cloud that follows the mouse. Clicking throws the particles outward before they settle again.
use: A dark landing page or hero wants a cursor that feels alive and reacts as people move and click.
avoid: WebGL runs continuously, it needs a sized parent, and touch screens have no pointer to follow.
a11y: Decorative canvas is aria-hidden and there is nothing to operate; motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A black stage scattered with very small white dots that bunch into a bright, swirling cloud around the pointer. Elsewhere the specks are sparse and faint, so the effect reads as a trail rather than a filled shape.
behaves: The swarm flows and curls continuously on its own while the pointer moves; the cloud thickens and stretches with cursor speed. Hovering a button rings it with circulating particles, and a click bursts them outward.
customise: Count, size, shape, colours, spread, speed, swirl, trail, idle behaviour and click effect are props; the fluid simulation itself needs a source edit.
weight: heavy: WebGL frame loop with a fluid simulation and up to 800 particles every frame.
demo: Headline "Ship the interface tonight", subline and two pill buttons on black.
polishWhy: Dense, believable motion; the idle specks are faint enough to look like leftover noise.
